message.content:
Here are a few highly regarded documentaries that explore global warming and climate change:

| Title | Year | Synopsis |
|-------|------|----------|
| **“An Inconvenient Truth”** | 2006 | Former Vice‑President Al Gore presents a comprehensive overview of climate science, the evidence for global warming, and the political challenges to addressing it. |
| **“An Inconvenient Sequel: Truth to Power”** | 2017 | A follow‑up to the original film, this documentary examines progress (or lack thereof) since 2006, focusing on policy, activism, and the role of media. |
| **“Before the Flood”** | 2016 | Leonardo DiCaprio travels around the world to witness the impacts of climate change, interviewing scientists, activists, and leaders while exploring solutions. |
| **“Climate Change: The Facts”** | 2019 | A BBC production that uses data visualizations and expert interviews to explain the science behind global warming and its socioeconomic consequences. |
| **“The 11th Hour”** | 2007 | Produced by Leonardo DiCaprio, this film features a panel of scientists and environmentalists discussing the state of the planet and what can be done to mitigate climate change. |

All of these films are available on major streaming platforms such as Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, Hulu, or YouTube (sometimes for free with ads). If you’d like more details on a specific documentary—such as runtime, availability, or key takeaways—just let me know!
